selected_top_5.reasoning: Threats appear continuously over time and must be cleared before they damage the player's defensive resource pool, creating a defense-under-pressure loop closest to arcade wave defense.
Primary play is repeated rapid clicking/tapping on targets in real time, making direct pointer interaction the dominant mechanic even though it is more arcade-oriented than idle/incremental clickers.
The player survives as long as possible against increasing pressure, with failure defined by losing all lives rather than completing fixed stages.
The game is confined to a single arena-like screen where threats move freely and are eliminated through immediate action, but there is no melee combat or character-versus-character fighting system.
Glowing targets, explosion particles, GIF reactions, and punchy audiovisual feedback give the game a tactile satisfying-play quality, though this is presentation-adjacent rather than the main genre.

uncertainty_notes: The category universe does not contain a direct 'arcade shooter gallery' or 'target tapping game' label, so the closest available categories were used.
Tower defense was considered because of the defense framing, but the lack of tower placement or lane strategy makes it a weaker fit than Wave defense game.
Clicker game is only a partial fit because this title is reflex/action-based rather than idle or progression-clicker focused.
